parts:
Hi Vincent,

This is Arpita, from Maja bucan's lab from the University of Pennsylvania. We once met on a skype call.
First, I want to thank you for developing such an excellent platform to analyse actigraphy data. It's very helpful.
I have a few questions about GGIR. 
i) Is it only processing raw data or it can process epoch level data(i.e 1min epoch or 5min epoch)?
ii) Does it impute gforce and count data both?
iii) Can we change manually the non wear period or is there any parameter to set non wear period hours?

Thank you,
Arpita

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] RAW data and epoch level dats
parts:
Hi Arpita, see my answers below.

‐‐‐‐‐‐‐ Original Message ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐

On Wednesday 3 June 2020 23:56, Arpita Ghorai <arpita...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Vincent,

This is Arpita, from Maja bucan's lab from the University of Pennsylvania. We once met on a skype call.
First, I want to thank you for developing such an excellent platform to analyse actigraphy data. It's very helpful.
I have a few questions about GGIR. 
i) Is it only processing raw data or it can process epoch level data(i.e 1min epoch or 5min epoch)?

> No, but with some R skills it is possible to imitate GGIR's milestone data (inside the meta/basic folder) with your 1 min or 5 minute epoch data. It is not ideal, but I understand that if there is no raw data then this could be a option. I can develop this as part of a paid consultancy, if you are interested.
ii) Does it impute gforce and count data both?
> GGIR imputes epoch level signal features, some of which are expressed in g-units. GGIR does not impute the raw data directly.
iii) Can we change manually the non wear period or is there any parameter to set non wear period hours?

> There are various options in GGIR to specify the study protocol and by that to exclude X number of hours at beginning or end. See documentation for function g.part2 and the function vignette. However, telling GGIR what specific periods of time in each individual it should consider as non-wear (2am to 4am in person A on day X) is not possible....but this can be done with some R coding skills, because this is more of a study specific need. I can do this as a paid consultancy if you are interested.
Thank you,
Arpita
